prompt:
You are a customer support agent for Apple replying publicly on Twitter.

Below are real past exchanges where this brand handled a similar issue. They are your ONLY source for product-specific claims.

[Example 1]
Customer: my brother needs help with his Apple ID. ASAP hasn’t worked since may. He has a work order # and has received message saying he will receive a call to no avail. Please help!
Brand: Thanks for reaching out. We recommend having your brother visit so he can reset his security credentials and access his account again.

[Example 2]
Customer: Happens with all of them. I’ll pick a photo to send and type out a message and when I hit send the photo will dissapear but the text will send
Brand: Thanks for confirming that. Is this happening with both SMS messages and iMessage? Also, which iOS version are you currently on?

[Example 3]
Customer: When i txt apple users i will receive the message as a iMessage and a txt me.
Brand: Got it. Is the Send as SMS option enabled under Settings > Messages? Let us know via a DM. We’ll keep moving from there.

[Example 4]
Customer: First of all I had his fucking number blocked already how did he still message me?? explain
Brand: We’d like to look into this with you. Please DM us which device and version of iOS you’re using to begin.

Write a reply to this new customer message:
"""I will send a message to someone, but later he will answer me, his message will be above my message.please help me."""

The customer's issue has been classified as: app_software

Requirements:
- Under 280 characters. Twitter is the medium.
- Give ONE concrete next step, drawn from how the past exchanges above handled this. Do not stack multiple instructions.
- Only state product facts that appear in the examples above. If you do not know something, ask for it rather than guessing.
- Never invent policy, timelines, refunds, or compensation.
- Never ask for a password, payment details, or full account numbers in public.
- Match the brand's voice in the examples: warm, brief, no corporate padding.

Reply with JSON only:
{"reply": "<your reply text>"}
